name: @w6w-apps/judgeme
description: Collect, moderate and reply to Judge.me product reviews, and manage reviewers, shop settings and webhooks.

w6w.longDescription:
Judge.me is an ecommerce product-reviews platform used mainly by Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce stores. This app covers the review lifecycle a workflow needs: list, fetch, count and create reviews, and publish or hide (curate) them once they're in. It also manages the reviewer record behind each review — looked up by Judge.me's internal id, the store platform's external id, or email — and can submit the data requests Judge.me's own GDPR/CCPA tooling expects.

Beyond reviews themselves, it covers the surfaces a store operator manages alongside them: public and private replies (the latter emails the reviewer without publishing anything), the shop's own Judge.me-held profile and settings, and webhooks for reacting to review events instead of polling.

Judge.me's storefront widgets (the HTML fragments a theme embeds directly on product pages) are a display concern, not a workflow operation, and are deliberately out of scope here — as is the separate paid Checkout Comments add-on. Judge.me's own OpenAPI document also documents a second, OAuth2-based credential, but never publishes the token endpoint it would need — this app authenticates with an API key instead, which is the credential Judge.me's own document fully specifies.
